utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, you agreed that you were interviewed by the US authorities in relation to your immigration fraud conviction. Do you recall that the first interview was videotaped?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Do you dispute that the first video was -- the first interview was videotaped? And this was an interview on 15 October 2004.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't dispute it, but I don't remember that it was videotaped.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, I was asking you before the break about a possible sighting of Jankovic, Petrovic, and Momir Nikolic near Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And if we get 65 ter document 32111 on the monitor, page 11, and we look at the last paragraph, and I'll just note for everybody that the B/C/S and English of this document correspond, the pages and paragraphs on each page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is one of the pages from the reports of the interviews that the US authorities conducted with you. And if we look at the last paragraph of this -- of this page, we see in the second sentence it states: "Blagojevic claimed that he observed Jankovic, Petrovic, and Momir Nikolic in an UNPROFOR vehicle near Konjevic Polje when Blagojevic was following the busloads of Muslim prisoners to Zvornik." Now I acknowledge that you link this to the busload -- following the buses of prisoners to Zvornik, but I'm going suggest to you that, in fact, you saw them on the UN vehicle on 13 July. And the Chamber has heard evidence from, firstly, Momir Nikolic on this point, who stated -- and I'll set this out before I pose my question. He stated at transcript page 11944, and this is 3 June 2013, the following: "Q. Thank you. Now moving on, did you make another journey down the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road later that same day, 13 July? "A. Yes, I did go one more time. "Q. Let me stop you and just ask: Can you tell us who you went with and what vehicle you went in? "A. I went the same day in the afternoon with the commander of the military police, Mirko Jankovic, and the deputy commander of the Bratunac Brigade military police, Milo Petrovic, and we went in an APC of the UNPROFOR or, rather, of the DutchBat, because during that day and earlier, in the Bratunac Brigade, we did have a few APCs available to us." If we then look to Mile Petrovic's testimony on this, and this can be found from the transcript of 9 February 2015, pages 31324 to 31325: "Q. You agree with Nikolic that you travelled on the 13th July in an APC from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje? "A. Yes, I travelled with him and Mirko. "Q. Mirko Jankovic? "A. Yes. "Q. This was a stolen UN APC; right? "A. Yes. "Q. It was white and it had UN markings on it in big black letters; yes? "A. Correct." Sir, in light of this evidence that the Chamber's heard, are you willing to accept that it's possible that your sighting of these three on the UN vehicle near Konjevic Polje happened on 13 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, I maintain with full responsibility. No, I did not see them that day in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And you maintain, as you say in your statement, that you're completely certain you did not see Momir Nikolic on 13 July?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I maintain that I did not see him on that day when we were escorting General Mladic in Konjevic Polje. Maybe he was in Konjevic Polje, but I did not see him on that day when we were escorting General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Did you, as reported by the US authorities, see these three on an APC at all near Konjevic Polje, on any date?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No. I said I had heard that they had been in Konjevic Polje on an UNPROFOR APC, Mile Petrovic, Momir Nikolic, but I did not see them. I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So where it states in the bottom paragraph of page 11 that you claimed that you observed these three on the UN vehicle, you are disputing that. You're saying that's incorrect?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you some questions about a location called Nova Kasaba, which is beside a football field. Are you aware of that location?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: When you were escorting General Mladic on 13 July, you stopped there with him and he spoke to prisoners at the field; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I'm going to play what you told the US agents about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we could get 65 ter 32112, clip 13, and this should be time codes 01:07:18 to 01:09:46. And I note the -- for the transcript of this video, which is one transcript with B/C/S and English in it together, this is on pages 63 through to 65. And, Your Honours, just because the transcript has both B/C/S and English in it, and everything is being translated to English, and because the booths have the transcript with the clips marked, I am in your hands as to whether we need to play this twice or whether it will be sufficient to play it once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that if -- what we need, of course, is the English transcript. I am also looking at the parties. If it is a question-and-answer situation in which we can follow the English and where the B/C/S can be followed especially by the Defence, then I think - but I'm just consulting my colleagues - that we could play it once. And if there's any challenge to the accuracy or the -- of the transcript, then we'll hear that later. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you. So if we could now play clip 13.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could you give us a second to find 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we could re-start. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And wait for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And on the transcript, this is halfway down page 63 of the transcript that the booths have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And could you state for the record where we start with the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: The time code is 01:07:18 seconds. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: "And you said you stopped at the soccer pitch at Nova Kasaba?" "Yes. "Were the prisoners on that pitch at the time? "Yes. "And who was securing those prisoners? "Also the army. Also army and the police. I don't know whether these police actually were members of the special police unit. I don't know. "Okay. And did Mladic address these prisoners? "Yes, he did. "Can you remember what was said at that location? "Almost the same. "How long did you remain there? "Same. "And from there you continue on to Vlasenica? "Yes. "Is that to the Drina Corps headquarters? "Yes. Yes, but we stop once before the corps."

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: We can pause it there. Thank you. And we've stopped at 1:08:34 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, you heard what was stated there. When you state that Mladic --

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now I'll just check for Your Honours. Did that come through clearly? You weren't able to follow. Perhaps because in the original video it is all being translated into English, I wonder if it's better to just play the video with the volume up so that we can hear it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I turned up my volume already, because we can do that ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Apologies. Volume up on the video without interpretation, because there is English being provided throughout the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we have it now on the record. We play it once again now without translation so that we can follow every word as spoken in English. And any B/C/S-speaking person can follow the conversation as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we first ask the witness if he recognise himself in this video.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please play it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "And you said you stopped at the soccer pitch at Nova Kasaba? "Yes. "Were there prisoners on that pitch at the time? "Yes. "And who was securing those prisoners? "Also the army. Also army and the police. I don't know whether this police actually were members of the special police unit, I don't know. "Okay. And did Mladic address these prisoners? "Yes, he did. "Can you remember what was said at that location? "Almost the same. "How long did you remain there? "Same. "Okay. And from there you continue on to Vlasenica? "Yes "And is that to the Drina Corps headquarters?"

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Okay. We can stop there. Thank you. And I note we stopped at 1 hour, 8 minutes, and 25 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: First, Mr. Blagojevic, you mention that what he said to the prisoners was the same. You're meaning that it's the same as what he said to the prisoners at Sandici meadow; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And the prisoners were sitting down on the football field; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: When you say the army was guarding them, you mean the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Did you see Mladic order some of the VRS soldiers to register the prisoners there at Nova Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Did you see any mistreatment of the Muslim prisoners at Nova Kasaba on 13 July when you stopped there?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, here is what one of the Muslim prisoners who was present at Nova Kasaba on that day said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And for Your Honours, this is transcript page 9567. "Q. Now we've been talking about this incident of a prisoner being shot at the Nova Kasaba football field. Can you tell us in your own words what is -- as far as you remember it, what happened? "A. Well, while Mladic was there holding a speech, one of the youths stood up. I don't know why he stood up. At any rate, the Serbian soldiers removed him from the rows where we were seated. He was toward the end of the row. He started beating him with rifle-butts and kicking him, and then one of them shot him from a rifle. His body was thrown into a nearby ditch. Mladic was present but didn't react at all. We were told -- they told us that if anyone of us should behave this way, we would be killed."

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, in your statement, you describe with some detail the other events during the escort mission with Mladic, but you don't describe the events at Nova Kasaba, do you? And to clarify, I'm talking about your statement which is now admitted into evidence under the number D922.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I maintain with full responsibility that this incident did not happen while General Mladic and I were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to repeat my question. My question was: You describe the other incidents during the escort mission with General Mladic on 13 July with detail, but you don't describe this stop during the escort mission, do you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: In my statement, I said that from Bratunac to Vlasenica, General Mladic made two stops. The first was in the sector of Sandici, and the second one was in Nova Kasaba, at the football field.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, if I give you a copy of your statement, would you like to show us where you describe the events at Nova Kasaba on 13 July, or are you willing to accept that there is no description? There is only one mention of Nova Kasaba with no detail added at all.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I've already mentioned that one stop was made in Sandici, he addressed people there, and he addressed Muslim prisoners in Kasaba approximately with the same words, as in Sandici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you're now asked about the statement you gave to the Mladic Defence, not about the statement you gave to the American investigators. And the question is whether have you an explanation why you don't give any details about stopping in Nova Kasaba and Mr. Mladic addressing any Muslim persons held in -- on the football pitch. That's the question, why this does not appear in any detail any further in your statement you've given to the Mladic Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct. But I'm telling you, I have no intention of concealing anything. Quite simply, these were two stops. Now why I didn't mention that, I mentioned the sports field but I did not mention in detail what happened during this address by General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to put it to you that you don't provide the detail of what happened at Nova Kasaba because this Bosnian Muslim's evidence is true, that the killing did occur there and that Mladic was there while it happened. That is the reason that you don't provide any description of the events at Nova Kasaba on 13 July in your statement to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I am repeating to you yet again, while at the stadium, while General Mladic was there, not a single incident occurred. The general wouldn't have allowed that. Again, I repeat, that incident did not occur while the general and I were there at the sports field. I state that with full responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, sir, you said before that you did not see Mladic ordering VRS soldiers to register the prisoners. Do you realise that Zoran Malinic, the head of the 65th Protection Regiment testified -- provided evidence that Mladic did instruct the VRS soldiers at Nova Kasaba on 13 July to register the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And for Your Honours, I will put the reference on the transcript. It's P155, page 65 in e-court, transcript page 15376.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So, sir, I will repeat my question. Do you realise that Zoran Malinic, the head of the 65th Protection Regiment, said that Mladic did order VRS soldiers to register the prisoners? Do you accept that that happened?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, but I accept that that is possible, that that happened. But I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Zoran Malinic also said that a Bosnian Muslim prisoner was killed at Nova Kasaba on 13 July. So do you accept that is also possible and that you may have forgotten about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I find that question unclear. Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Zoran Malinic also said that a Bosnian Muslim prisoner was killed at Nova Kasaba on 13 July, and I would note that the Prosecution disputes the details of his account of this, but he says that that occurred. Do you accept that it is possible that that occurred while you and General Mladic were at Nova Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already answered that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it would be fair to the witness to quote that part of Mr. Malinic's statement, if it's already being used.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Certainly. If Your Honours would like, I'm happy to go to that evidence. Although I'm not sure that I -- I feel the witness's position may already be clear on this issue, but since the Defence has asked, I'd go to the statement -- I'd go to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you have no problems in doing that. Otherwise, of course, the Defence could do it in re-examination. But if you're willing to do it, it may speed up ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honour's suggestion is even more preferable. I think the witness's position is clear. If you just give me one second to check the transcript. In fact, I haven't received an answer to this question. So I'll state it, and if the Defence wants to bring up the transcript for additional details, of course, that's -- they're entitled to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: But I'll just get an answer from you, sir. Do you accept, based on Zoran Malinic's account, that it is possible that a Bosnian Muslim prisoner was killed at Nova Kasaba on 13 July while yourself and Mladic were there?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I repeat to you yet again, while I was there at the stadium, while the general was there, not a single bullet was fired. That is to say, it could be heard. I am not challenging whether that happened before or afterwards, but while we were at the stadium in Kasaba, there was not a single gun-shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll move on. Sir, when you --

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Unless Your Honours have additional questions on that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: When you finished escorting Mladic on 13 July, you came back to the Bratunac Brigade headquarters; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And when you returned, Momir Nikolic ordered you to go and guard prisoners at the Vuk Karadzic school in Bratunac; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall whether it's Momir Nikolic or Mirko Jankovic. I don't remember who it was that said that. Now was it Momir Nikolic or Mirko Jankovic? I cannot say that to you for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Can we get 65 ter document 32111, page 18. Thank you. This document should still be on the screen. If we go to page 18, the second-last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: While this comes up, let me ask the following: Mr. Blagojevic, were you ordered to guard prisoners at the Vuk Karadzic school? By whomever.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What do you mean, in writing or orally?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In whichever way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm telling you, when we returned from the escort, it was perhaps 11.00 or 12.00 at night when we arrived before the command of the military police. I cannot remember. I cannot remember for sure whether it was Jankovic, the commander of the military police, or Momir Nikolic that told us to go in front of the Vuk Karadzic school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Witness, did you go to the Vuk Karadzic school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And that was an order given by somebody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we look at the second-last paragraph of this page, it states: "Asked if he saw people being loaded on buses, Blagojevic stated he did not see prisoners on buses at that time, but did see them following the escort of Mladic after returning to Bratunac, when he was ordered by Nikolic to guard the school." Does that refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm telling you yet again, I cannot say for sure whether it was Nikolic that said that or Jankovic. I cannot be 100 per cent certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So, in fact, you can't be certain whether you saw Momir Nikolic on 13 July or not, can you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And you cannot be sure -- actually, let me go to what you say in your statement to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we look at paragraph 12. And this is now D922. If we could get -- and this is page 3 of the statement, paragraph 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: The second sentence which is just coming up reads: "What I am completely certain of is that on that day, 13 July, I did not see Momir Nikolic, whom I knew very well personally." In fact, you did see Momir Nikolic on 13 July, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I told you already I'm not sure whether it was Jankovic that told us or Nikolic. That is to say, I'm not sure, I cannot remember, when we returned from the escort, whether it was Jankovic that told us or Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And that sentence is incorrect when it says that you are completely certain that on that day, 13 July, you did not see Momir Nikolic, who knew -- you knew very well personally. It's not correct, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Objection. This is a misquote. The sentence says: "I am sure that day in Konjevic Polje," and my learned friend did not quote that, "I did not see Momir Nikolic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, that's not what the statement in English says, unless there's any -- any translation issue, we'll have that verified. But as a matter of fact, Mr. Gillett is quoting the English version of the statement accurately, and I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please read before you object, Mr. Stojanovic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, that sentence, and I'll read it again, in your statement at paragraph 12: "What I am completely certain of is that on that day, 13 July, I did not see Momir Nikolic, whom I knew very well personally," is not correct. You're not completely certain of that, are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm just going to repeat once again that I think obviously we have a problem here. In the English translation this word is missing, and in the B/C/S it doesn't sound that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's have a look at --

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I'm looking at the B/C/S now and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there's a fair chance that there is a translation issue there because in the B/C/S, I see in the second sentence which refers to the 13th of July also at least refers to Konjevic Polje and in the same sentence refers to Momir Nikolic. So it should be verified very carefully.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, sir, if I could --

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Unless Your Honours have any further questions on that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but I have one observation. Mr. Stojanovic, if you would take care that you present proper translations rather than to start objecting to what Mr. Gillett does. As a matter of fact, objecting to him using the material you have provided which is inaccurate, you should have verified it first before you came to court instead of creating problems for Mr. Gillett. Please proceed, Mr. Gillett. We have no further questions on the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If I could jump back in time to earlier on 13 July, you've mentioned the events at Sandici meadow while you were escorting Mladic along the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road. Now, in your statement, you say that Mladic spoke to the prisoners at Sandici and that you could hear everything he was saying; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And when Mladic was speaking to the prisoners, he told them to get their fellow Bosnian Muslims to surrender from the surrounding area; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: He also told them that they had been cheated by Naser Oric; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And that they had been cheated by the president of Bosnia, who I take it you meant Izetbegovic; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we look at paragraph 8 of your statement, which I hope is translated correctly, we see your description of the Mladic speech to the prisoners at Sandici. Here you say --

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And this should be on -- over the page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And this is the -- halfway through the paragraph, you say: "The general addressed them in a very conciliatory voice, telling them not be afraid, as they would be exchanged for the imprisoned Serbs, and asked them if anyone was ill and needed to see a doctor. As far as I remember, none of them responded. I was in direct proximity and heard all of this." You don't mention there that Mladic told the prisoners to call their fellow Bosnian Muslims to surrender from the surrounding area, do you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't mention that. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, you know that most of the Muslims who surrendered that day were then taken and executed at locations such as Kravica warehouse in Bratunac and Zvornik; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: How many prisoners did you see at Sandici meadow; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't counting them. I cannot say now. Well, I don't know. I don't know exactly how many. In my estimate, well, I stated it was 100. Perhaps it was more than that, but they were in a group. So quite simply, I mean, I wasn't counting and I did not have time to -- I mean, quite simply, we had to provide security there at that location where the general was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Could we get 65 ter 32111. This is, again, the report of the investigations by the US authorities. And if we go to page 19, the second paragraph. If we could get English. I'm seeing only B/C/S on the second half of the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: The third paragraph down states: "Going towards Bratunac, on the right (south), there was a huge meadow at Sandici where people who surrendered from the Muslim column in the hills travelling to Tuzla were being held. There were VRS soldiers and he believes also special police units present guarding the prisoners. Blagojevic named their commander as Ljubisa Boroc. "Blagojevic stated he was unsure of the number of prisoners being held there, possibly 500 to 1.000. There were only men, as the women and children had surrendered in Potocari. He identified the men as Muslims from Srebrenica, and when questioned on how he knew this, he affirmed that General Mladic referred to them as such." Does that refresh your memory that there was a group of between 500 to 1.000 prisoners at Sandici?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I've said, it's possible there were from 300 to 500 to 1.000. I mean, I don't know. They were out there in the meadow. Now how many of them were there, I cannot tell you exactly. I cannot give you an exact figure. It's possible that there were up to 500, around 500.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You state here it's possible there were up to 1.000. Do you accept that there could have been that many, or do you dispute that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I dispute that, that it was up to 1.000. But, again, I'm telling you, I cannot say exactly whether there were 300, whether there were 500, whether there were 400. It's possible that there were up to 500. Around 500.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, the -- I'm going to ask you about the special police commander that you mention.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Could we get the 65 ter 18954 on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: While this comes up, I would like to ask the witness the following. You said - this can be found on page 66, lines 21 and 22 - "Well, I've said it's possible there were from 3- to 500 to 1.000." Five lines you say: "I dispute that, that it was up to 1.000." What is true? To dispute 1.000 after having said it's possible that there were up to 1.000?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I dispute that there were 1.000 of them. In terms of my visual viewing of that meadow. I dispute that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Why did you first say "it's possible that there were from 300 to 500 to 1.000"? That is what you said before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm telling you, quite simply, in that meadow, at first sight, I mean, that's what it was like, that there were lots of them. Now, as for this figure, what I said, I'm not sure. But I'm telling you now, now going back, replaying these memories, I doubt that there were more than 500 of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I don't think that is correct to say playing memories. It's a very serious matter. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, do you recognise the person in this picture?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Who is it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Ljubisa Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And he's the special police commander you saw at Sandici; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I think he was. Special police commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: To clarify, you think he was the police commander, special police commander, you saw at Sandici. Did I understand you right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I think it's him. I'm not 100 per cent sure. But the special police was the special police for us. They had blue uniforms. They didn't have uniforms like the army. They had different uniforms and they were called special police. And I think that he was commander of that special police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I take the witness back to the number issue. You say -- you don't know exactly, but anywhere within 300 and 500, that's what you consider a fair possibility, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Why did you say in your statement that there were around 100?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I'm telling you yet again, I wasn't counting them, but when I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to stop you there. You explained all that. You earlier said up to 1.000 and now you say, Well, today I tell you 300 to 500. That's approximately what had you to think in -- of. In your statement, you say 100, "around 100," which is a considerably lower number compared to what you tell us today. And I'm asking you for an explanation as why you mentioned "around 100," whereas today you tell us that it was three to five times as much as what you said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know now why I said that, 100.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you attested to that. You told us that that is the truth. You corrected minor details in your statement. Why didn't you correct this one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, the person on the screen in front of you - and I'm referring obviously to the man in the foreground - he is the special police commander that you referred to or is referred to in the report as Ljubisa Boroc that I just mentioned. It is, in fact, Ljubomir Borovcanin, correct, who is shown in this picture?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Could I tender this picture, which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: -- is 18954 for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number would be P7185.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, sir, he was present when yourself and Mladic were at Sandici meadow; correct? And I'm talking about Ljubomir Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No. As far as I can remember, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You realise that shortly after you and Mladic stopped at Sandici meadow, prisoners from there, Muslim prisoners, were taken and executed at Kravica warehouse; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I don't know where they were taken. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, you've mentioned that you know and you knew in July 1995 Mile Petrovic; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Did you hear about him killing Muslim prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I heard that in Momir Nikolic's statement, the one that I read, that he said that he had killed some Muslims in Konjevic Polje. That is to say, that is something I heard and read from Momir Nikolic's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: When did you read the statement?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: While I was in America. I read it on the computer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Can you recall what year?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I am not sure. Maybe 2004, 2005. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm about to move to a new topic. I'm wondering how close we are to the break as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are extremely close to the break. It's time for a break. Witness, we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have another matter where we are still waiting for information that relates to the testimony of Slavko Puhalic. During his testimony on 12th of February of this year, D899, which is a video, was marked for identification, pending information from the Defence including the date and shooting location of the video and the number of sequences included in the video. You can find that at transcript pages 31649 to 651. And the question is whether the Defence is now in a position to provide this information. And I do not immediately expect an answer, Mr. Lukic, but if that answer could be given this week, we would appreciate that. I could also set a deadline. The deadline is the 9th of March, next Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gillett, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, we've discussed earlier that you were ordered to go and guard the Vuk Karadzic school in Bratunac on the evening of 13 July. And other military police from the Bratunac Brigade went with you to carry out this guard duty; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Can you remember which ones went with you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I remember a number, but not all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Can you remember any of the names of the military police that went with you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was a driver with me, Milovan Mitrovic. The commander of the vehicle, Slobodan Mijatovic. I think there was Pero Antolic [as interpreted], Borivoje Jakovljevic. And I don't remember the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Would that be Pero Andric?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: When you arrived at the Vuk Karadzic school, were there other military police or VRS members already present?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Do you know who they were?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: You mean the names? Are you asking the names of military police or the troops?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If you know any of the names of any of the VRS members that were present when you arrived at the Vuk Karadzic school, could you tell us.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember the names exactly, but there was also the civilian police. The police in blue uniform was there, not only the army police. I really don't remember the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Do you remember if the military police were from the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: When you went to carry out this guard duty with your fellow members of your military police group that you've mentioned, you were armed; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And where were you located when you were carrying out this guard duty?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Can I get a sketch of the school, a drawing of the schoolhouse and the area around it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: How about I suggest that you were located in front of the Vuk Karadzic school. Would that -- does that sound correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Before the school but not exactly outside the school. Not directly in front of the school, but more towards the municipal building, to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: While you were there, armed Bosnian Serbs took Muslim prisoners off buses and killed them behind the Vuk Karadzic school; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: While you were present on the evening, the night of 13 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No. No, I did not see any killings.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Are you aware whether you saw or heard of any armed Bosnian Serbs taking Muslim prisoners off the buses and killing them behind the Vuk Karadzic school on 13 July?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I heard that, but I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we could get 65 ter document 32111. Again, this is the report of the US investigation. And if we go to page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I meanwhile ask a clarification. You said: "I heard that, but I didn't see it." Did you hear that it happened later on? Or did you hear shots being fired? What did you mean by "I heard that"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Later on, I heard that some men had taken Muslims out and killed them. And the next morning, I saw a couple of corpses outside the school. But I didn't see the fact. We arrived at the school perhaps around midnight. And the next morning, at sunrise, I saw outside the school, if you are facing the school, then to the right side, there were four or five dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you hear any shots being fired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During the night? Yes, I heard shots several times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Shots from nearby?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Did some of the shots that you heard come from inside the Vuk Karadzic school?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I'll now read an excerpt from the report, which is still on the monitor, and I'm starting five lines down, where it says: "After the fall of Srebrenica, Blagojevic was assigned to General Mladic's security detail for the following 12 to 24 hours. When this detail was completed, Blagojevic and eight other military policemen were ordered to assist in securing the Muslim prisoners at the elementary school in Bratunac. Blagojevic stated that when he came on to the scene that evening, he observed approximately 20 to 30 buses lined up on the road in front of the school and they extended down to the soccer stadium. "Blagojevic described the elementary school, grades 1 through 8, as a three-storey structure with classrooms on each floor. Blagojevic did not enter the school while the prisoners were there. Blagojevic claimed that he and the eight other military policemen were in a truck in front of the school guarding the premises. Throughout the evening, Blagojevic observed armed Bosnian Serb civilians taking prisoners off the buses, some being struck with the butt of their rifles as they were being led behind the elementary school."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're reading, Mr. Gillett.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: "Blagojevic would then hear several gun-shots and the civilians would return without the prisoners. Also during the evening, Blagojevic heard automatic weapons fire coming from inside the elementary school. He claimed that many of the Muslim prisoners may have tried to escape. Blagojevic stated that he entered the school the next morning and saw the bodies of 10 to 15 Muslim men in a second-floor hallway that were killed."

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, you say here that you heard gun-fire from inside the school and that the following day you saw ten to 15 Muslim men in a second-floor hallway that were killed. Did you see which armed Bosnian Serbs entered the school and killed the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see it. I heard gun-fire. I don't know how much. It was early in the morning. I was tired because we had been kept busy with escorting the general the whole previous day, but I was woken up by sounds of gun-fire, maybe around 2.00 or 3.00 a.m., and there was gun-fire from inside the school, and we heard that there had been an attempt by the Muslims to escape.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You were on guard duty. Did you attempt to ascertain who was firing the guns inside the school?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: We actually got the task to guard the civilians in Bratunac because there were many captured Muslims there. That's what we were told. And there were few army troops because our army units had nearly all been transferred to Zepa, so there were few soldiers on guard duty with the police. And I also heard that civilian and military police went from house to house and rounded up younger and not-so-young men to guard those Muslims in the school and around the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You haven't answered my question, which was: You were guarding the Vuk Karadzic school, and I note that you were armed. Did you attempt to ascertain who was firing the guns from inside the school?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No. No, I did not have that authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Who gave you the authority to fire the Browning machine-gun at the window of the school when you claimed that a Muslim tried to escape?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I said clearly that I did not shoot. The Browning gun was used that night, but I didn't shoot, although I was convicted for it. While in the escort detail of General Mladic, I manned the Browning gun. The Browning gun did open fire at the school that night, but I'm not the one who fired it, and I don't feel guilty of that. I said that at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Who was the one that fired it then? According to you.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know who fired. When this gun-fire was heard around 2.00 or 3.00 a.m., when there was automatic gun-fire from the school, I had just fallen asleep. I was by the Browning gun. And, later on, I walked, like when you go from the station towards the school, I took a walk to the right up to the municipal building.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, you've mentioned a number of killings at the Vuk Karadzic school. Did you report these killings up the chain of command? And I'm talking about the killings on the evening of 13 July.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I think the superiors knew that. I wasn't alone there. No, I did not report it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I seek clarification of one of your previous answers. When that Browning gun was fired, had you been away at that moment? Is that how we have to understand it? Or were asleep next to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I told you, when there was this gun-fire, automatic fire from the school from infantry weapons, when the Muslims tried to escape, fire was opened. That's what I was told. They said, The Muslims are trying to escape, and that's when the fire was opened. I then woke up, and perhaps ten minutes later, I got off the Pinzgauer on which the Browning gun was mounted, and I took a walk towards the municipal building, to the right of the school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you were there to guard? Then there's firing from within the school? You wake up and you say, Let's take a walk. Is that how I have to understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I took a walk perhaps half an hour later because this gun-fire was short. It wasn't a long time. I don't know how long exactly, but it woke me up. It jolted me out of sleep. But then everything was quiet. And I took a walk later. I wasn't walking when the gun-fire was heard. Did you understand me now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I understand you now. And I also noticed that where you earlier said after approximately ten minutes, you now say after approximately half an hour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how long exactly it was, 10, 15 minutes, but the gun-fire had stopped. Everything was quiet. There was no noise whatsoever. Whether it was ten or 15 or 20 minutes, I don't know. In any case, there was absolutely no gun-fire when I left the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you left the vehicle, you were there on guard duty? You left the weapon without anyone being in charge of that weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, there were other men there, both army members and military police. The vehicle was not left unattended.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But who was then in charge of a vehicle which was carrying a -- well, a relatively heavy weapon? Who was responsible for that weapon at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I don't know, because it's just that when we set off as a security detail for the general, they told me that I am in charge of the Browning, but they didn't say it like it was strictly my responsibility: You have to take care of it, et cetera. So when I left the vehicle, I literally went to stretch my legs, to shake off sleep. It's not only I who was tired. Other people were tired too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see all of that. I do hear your answers. But no one apparently then was in charge of the Browning at that point in time, because you were before, although you say not formally. But who then was this charge of this weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I left the vehicle. Anyone from the military police or an army member, if required, could use that weapon. It was not my personal weapon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just -- I probably didn't understand your answers to the Judge. You say you were asleep when you were woken up by gun-fire coming from the school.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, when the Browning was shot into the school, where were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was out there in the street, perhaps 100 or 150 metres away from the Browning gun.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's what the Judge had asked you, and I didn't think you answered that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Gillett.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, you realise that at least five witnesses gave evidence that you were the one that fired the Browning gun on 13 July at the Vuk Karadzic school in the incident that you've just described during your trial for crimes against humanity in Bosnia; right? You know that.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I repeat again: The Browning gun did fire. I didn't. It's true I was convicted before the court in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I said I've served my sentence but I don't feel guilty.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned --

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you returned from your walk and you had heard the Browning go off and you had been told to be in charge of the Browning, did you investigate as to who shot the gun?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I inquired, I asked who fired and the answer I got was: It's not -- no business of yours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks. Mr. Gillett.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Who gave you that answer?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, those military policemen and the army troops who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, you've mentioned killings inside the school. It's also true that that evening a mentally handicapped Bosnian Muslim prisoner was dragged off one of the buses parked outside the school by military police and killed; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You've mentioned killings inside the school. But it's also true that a Bosnian Muslim handicapped -- mentally handicapped man was dragged off one of the buses parked outside the school by military police and then killed; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't mention that. I said that I had heard shooting in the school, but I did not say anything about that handicapped person.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking whether you said that previously. I'm asking whether you know that that occurred on 13 July.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: The next morning, 14 July, you were still guarding with military police outside the Vuk Karadzic school; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And you stayed there until 3.00 or 4.00 in the afternoon guarding the school; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I stayed till the end, but I can't remember the exact time. But, yes, I did stay there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Would you accept that it would have been mid-afternoon, around 3.00 or 4.00 p.m. that you stayed there until before you headed with the convoy of buses towards Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I can agree with that, but I'm not sure about the time. It's possible. I don't know whether it was 2.00 or 3.00. I don't know about the time, but I agree with the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Can we get -- and I see the break coming, but if I could quickly ask this question. If we could get 65 ter document 32112. And this is the transcript -- if we could get the transcript page 87 of the first interview carried out with the US authorities, and I note there was an ICTY representative present at this interview as well. So that's page 87.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And I'll read the English, and I will put it to that you this is very clearly talking about 14 July. You say --

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sorry. If we could go back a page, to page 86 first. Thank you. The final line of this page says: "What time did you remain at the school that day?" And if we turn over to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: The next English is: "The whole day. The whole day next day until 3.00 or 4.00 in the afternoon," and that's the interpretation of your answer. So do you accept now that it was 3.00 or 4.00 in the afternoon that you stayed there until?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I said that, but concerning the time -- but I agree. I agree that it was 3.00 or 4.00. The time doesn't matter. It could have been 2.00 or 3.00 or 4.00. But if I said that, yes, it's possible. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Well, it's possible or you agree? Do you agree with what is said there, what you previously stated?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I cannot be 100 per cent sure about the time. I cannot give you the exact time. It was 20 years ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, 20 -- at a time of taking this statement, you also did not give an exact time. You said 3.00 or 4.00. Do you agree that it could have been 3.00 or 4.00? It's not an exact time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Are we close to the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we are beyond the break time as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I still do have further questions but I imagine [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if it would be a half a question, then we could consider --

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's more to be said. Okay. Then we'll adjourn for the day. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before we adjourn, Your Honour, just a small request, and I announced it to my colleagues in the OTP. I have a medical appointment tomorrow and I notified, if we don't finish today, I wanted to address you that if there is any need for re-direct, that will be handled by my colleague, Mr. Branko Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although it's quite uncommon, if the Prosecution has no objection to it -- Mr. Lukic has been present during the whole of the examination of the witness and the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: There's no objection from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then Mr. Branko Lukic is allowed to ask any questions in re-direct, if -- yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just one more sentence at the suggestion of Mr. Mladic. If the Prosecution does not have much more time and if they will show some understanding, maybe if they don't have much longer, we can finish perhaps today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, there's no way to finish today because I have commitments elsewhere as well. And apart from that, Mr. Gillett, how much time would you still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: It's about 15 or 20 minutes. It can vary according to the answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there's no way that we could finish today. Witness, we adjourn for the day. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30. Well, you know more or less how much more time there will be for cross-examination. It's expected that we'll conclude your testimony tomorrow and relatively early. Before you leave this courtroom, I'd like to instruct you - and you should take those instructions very seriously - instruct you not to speak or communicate in whatever way, with whomever, about your testimony, whether that is testimony you have given today or whether that is testimony still to be given tomorrow. If that's clear to you, you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 5th of March, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 5th day of March, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.19 p.m.,
